etymologyHint: A necklace 丨 adorned with three pieces of jade

components.note: 王 here is not 'king' but a simplified string of three jade discs threaded on a cord.
丶 is the extra dot added to distinguish 玉 (jade) from 王 (king), representing the gem itself.

example.english: This piece of jade is very beautiful.
example.fact: 玉 (jade) has long been treasured in Chinese culture as a symbol of purity and nobility.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 镇 originally referred to a heavy metal weight used to press something down, later extending to 'garrison town.'
真 (zhēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 镇's reading zhèn, differing only in tone.

example.fact: 镇 is a common word for a small town, usually smaller than a city (市) and larger than a village (村).

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 雪 belongs to the group of weather words built on 雨, since snow falls the way rain does.
彐 gives a sound distantly related to xuě, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 雪 combines with 下 to form 下雪 (xiàxuě), the standard way to say 'it's snowing' in Chinese.

example.english: We eat lunch at twelve o'clock.
example.fact: 午 rarely stands alone — it usually appears in words like 中午 (zhōngwǔ, 'noon'), 上午 (shàngwǔ, 'morning'), and 下午 (xiàwǔ, 'afternoon').

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 练 originally meant to boil and whiten silk thread, extending to 'to practice, to train' through repeated refinement.
柬 (jiǎn) gives a sound distantly related to liàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: He practices writing Chinese characters every day.
example.fact: 练 almost always appears in 练习 (liànxí, 'to practice'), one of the most common verbs for language learners.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — pressing close on someone's heels ties to 迫's meaning 'to press, to force.'
白 (bái) gives a sound distantly related to pò, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 迫 commonly appears in 紧迫 (jǐnpò, 'urgent, pressing') and 被迫 (bèipò, 'to be forced to'), both describing pressure to act.

components.note: 父 (father) — 爷 belongs to the family of words for male elders.
耶 (yé) gives the sound — an exact match with 爷's reading yé.

example.english: Grandpa is taking a walk in the park.
example.fact: 爷 is doubled to form 爷爷 (yéye, 'grandpa'), the paternal grandfather, distinct from 外公 for the maternal grandfather.

etymologyHint: A bamboo ⺮ tablet 扁; 扁 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) recalls the bamboo strips ancient texts were written on, tying 篇 to writing.
扁 pictures something flat and thin, like a bamboo tablet — fitting for a single sheet or chapter of writing.

example.fact: 篇 is the measure word for pieces of writing, like 一篇文章 (yī piān wénzhāng, 'an article') or 一篇日记 (a diary entry).

etymologyHint: Meat on the ribs of an animal

components.note: 冂 traces the outer outline of a cut of meat.
仌 depicts the muscle fibers or ribs inside, together forming a picture of a piece of meat.

example.fact: 肉 by itself often implies pork specifically in everyday speech, since other meats are usually named with an extra word, like 牛肉 (beef) or 鸡肉 (chicken).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘴 refers directly to the mouth, or a beak-like spout.
觜 (zī) gives a sound distantly related to zuǐ, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: He opened his mouth and smiled.
example.fact: 嘴 is the everyday word for 'mouth' in speech, while 口 is more common in formal or written contexts.

etymologyHint: A public 官 building where food 饣 is served; 官 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 饣 (food) points to a place where meals are served.
官 pictures an official hall or residence, giving 馆 its sense of a large public building.

example.english: We're going to the museum to see an exhibition.
example.fact: 馆 appears in many public-building words, like 博物馆 (bówùguǎn, 'museum'), 图书馆 (túshūguǎn, 'library'), and 餐馆 (cānguǎn, 'restaurant').

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 遍 relates to covering ground everywhere, or going through something from start to end.
扁 (biǎn) gives a sound close to biàn, sharing the same rhyme and differing mainly in tone.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zhè běn shū kàn le sān biàn.
example.english: I've read this book three times.
example.fact: 遍 is a measure word counting full repetitions of an action from beginning to end, like reading a book 三遍 (three times through).

etymologyHint: A plate or flat dish; an everyday item

components.note: 几 traces the outline of a simple stand or tray.
丶 marks the flat surface of the dish, an ordinary household object that gave 凡 its sense of 'common, everyday.'

example.pinyin: Tā shì gè píngfán de rén.
example.fact: 凡 rarely stands alone in modern Chinese — it commonly appears in 平凡 (píngfán, 'ordinary') and 凡是 (fánshì, 'whatever, every').

components.note: 石 (stone) — 础 names the stone base of a pillar or building.
出 (chū) gives a sound distantly related to chǔ, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 教育是国家发展的基础。
example.pinyin: Jiàoyù shì guójiā fāzhǎn de jīchǔ.
example.english: Education is the foundation of national development.
example.fact: 础 almost always appears together with 基 in 基础 (jīchǔ, 'foundation, basis'), rarely standing alone.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 洞 originally described water hollowing out a cave or hole in rock.
同 (tóng) gives a sound distantly related to dòng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shān lǐ yǒu yí gè hěn shēn de dòng.
example.english: There is a very deep cave in the mountain.
example.fact: 洞 names any hole or cavity, from a mountain cave (山洞) to a small hole in a piece of clothing.

components.note: 龹 pictures two hands working together.
㔾 depicts a person curled up, giving 卷 its meaning of rolling or curling something up.

example.fact: 卷 describes rolling something into a cylinder, as in 卷起来 (juǎn qǐlái, 'to roll up') or 卷发 (juǎnfà, 'curly hair').

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坦 describes flat, level ground.
旦 (dàn) gives a sound close to tǎn, sharing a related rhyme.

example.english: This road is very flat and smooth.
example.fact: 坦 usually appears in 平坦 (píngtǎn, 'flat, level'), describing smooth ground, or in 坦白 (tǎnbái, 'to be honest'), describing an open, candid manner.

components.note: The character traces the front view of an ox's head, with the top stroke and crossing lines representing its curved horns and ears.

example.pinyin: Nóngmín yǎng le hěn duō niú.
example.english: The farmer raises a lot of cows.
example.fact: 牛 is a general word for cattle, covering both cows and oxen, and appears in 牛奶 (niúnǎi, 'milk') and 牛肉 (niúròu, 'beef').

meanings: abbr. for Nanjing 南京[Nan2 jing1]

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a peaceful home under a roof relates to 宁's meaning 'calm, serene.'
丁 (dīng) gives a sound distantly related to níng, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 宁 is also used as an abbreviation for Nanjing (南京) in some contexts, alongside its core meaning 'calm, peaceful.'

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — early paper was made from silk and plant fibers, linking 纸 to the thread radical.
氏 (shì) gives a sound distantly related to zhǐ, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì zhāng zhǐ.
example.english: Please give me a piece of paper.
example.fact: 纸 is measured with 张 (zhāng), the same measure word used for other flat objects like photos and tables.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诸 originally related to speaking of many things.
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to zhū, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 诸 is a literary word for 'many, various,' most often seen in set expressions like 诸位 (zhūwèi, 'everyone present') and 诸如 (zhūrú, 'such as').

meanings: to teach; to train; to admonish

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 训 relates to teaching through spoken instruction.
川 (chuān) gives a sound distantly related to xùn, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: The teacher trains the students to play basketball.
example.fact: 训 usually appears in 训练 (xùnliàn, 'to train') and 培训 (péixùn, 'to train, cultivate'), both about building skills through practice.

etymologyHint: 厶 provides the meaning and pronunciation

components.note: 禾 (grain) — grain was one of the first things ancient people owned and kept for themselves.
厶 pictures something folded in on itself and hidden away, giving 私 its sense of 'private, personal, one's own.'

example.fact: 私 commonly appears in 私人 (sīrén, 'private, personal') and 自私 (zìsī, 'selfish').

components.note: 广 (shelter/building) — 庄 originally referred to farm buildings or a manor house.
壯 (zhuàng) gives a sound close to zhuāng, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.pinyin: Tā zhù zài yí gè xiǎo cūnzhuāng.
example.english: He lives in a small village.
example.fact: 庄 usually pairs with 村 to form 村庄 (cūnzhuāng, 'village'), and also names Zhuangzi (庄子), a famous ancient Chinese philosopher.

components.note: 礻 (spirit/altar) — ancestor worship at a family altar ties 祖 to the spirit radical.
且 (qiě) gives a sound distantly related to zǔ, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 祖 commonly appears in 祖先 (zǔxiān, 'ancestors') and 祖国 (zǔguó, 'homeland, motherland').

meanings: classifier: a trace (of smoke etc), a tiny bit etc
etymologyHint: Simplified form of 絲, two threads

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 丝 is a simplified picture of two twisted strands of silk thread.

example.pinyin: Tā chuān le yì tiáo sīchóu qúnzi.
example.fact: 丝 is the word for silk and fine thread, and gives its name to the ancient Silk Road, 丝绸之路 (Sīchóu zhī Lù).

components.note: 羽 (feather/wings) — flipping and turning relates to the flapping motion of wings.
番 (fān) gives the sound — an exact match with 翻's reading fān.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū fān dào dì shí yè.
example.english: Please turn the book to page ten.
example.fact: 翻 describes flipping or turning something over, as in 翻书 (fān shū, 'to flip through a book') or 翻译 (fānyì, 'to translate').

etymologyHint: A man with head 日 and hands 共 tormenting a deer 水

components.note: 日 here pictures a person's head.
共 pictures two hands; together with the shape below, they depict a violent struggle, giving 暴 its meaning 'violent, sudden.'

example.fact: 暴 describes something sudden and intense, as in 暴雨 (bàoyǔ, 'rainstorm') and 暴力 (bàolì, 'violence').

etymologyHint: Many trees 木 forming a forest

components.note: 木 (tree) is repeated three times, piling up to picture a dense forest.

example.fact: 森 almost always appears in 森林 (sēnlín, 'forest'), built from three copies of 木 (tree) stacked together to suggest abundance.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 塔 refers to a tall earthen or stone structure.
荅 (dá) gives a sound distantly related to tǎ, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 塔 names tower-like structures, from Buddhist pagodas (佛塔) to the Eiffel Tower (埃菲尔铁塔).

etymologyHint: A dog 犬 watching in the dark 黑

components.note: 黑 (black/dark) pictures nightfall.
犬 (dog) pictures a dog keeping silent watch in the dark, giving 默 its meaning 'silent, still.'

example.english: He kept silent the whole time.
example.fact: 默 commonly appears in 沉默 (chénmò, 'silence') and 默默 (mòmò, 'silently, quietly').

meanings: (bound form) to have in one's control

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 握 describes an action done with the hand: grasping tightly.
屋 (wū) gives a sound distantly related to wò, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 握 usually appears in 握手 (wòshǒu, 'to shake hands') and 把握 (bǎwò, 'to grasp, be sure of').

etymologyHint: A hand 又 doing tricks with a spear 戈

components.note: 又 (hand) shows a hand performing an action.
戈 (spear) — mock combat and stage tricks with weapons gave 戏 its meaning 'play, drama.'

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan kàn zhè zhǒng xì.
example.english: He likes watching this kind of opera.
example.fact: 戏 names traditional Chinese theater, as in 京剧 (Jīngjù, 'Peking opera'), and also appears in 游戏 (yóuxì, 'game').

etymologyHint: A place 阝 to hide when worried 急

components.note: 阝 (mound/place) suggests a hidden spot behind a hill.
急 (worried, urgent) suggests someone anxiously ducking out of sight, giving 隐 its meaning 'to hide, conceal.'

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ mìmì yǐncáng qǐlái le.
example.fact: 隐 usually appears in 隐藏 (yǐncáng, 'to hide') and 隐私 (yǐnsī, 'privacy').

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 熟 describes food that has been cooked thoroughly over fire.
孰 (shú) gives the sound — an exact match with 熟's reading shú.

example.fact: 熟 describes both cooked food and ripe fruit, and extends to 熟悉 (shúxi, 'familiar with'), describing people or places you know well.

meanings: used in 骨碌碌[gu1 lu4 lu4]

components.note: 冎 pictures a joint of bone.
⺼ (flesh) sits below, together giving 骨 its meaning 'bone.'

example.fact: 骨 combines with 头 to form 骨头 (gǔtou, 'bone'), the everyday word used at the dinner table and at the doctor's office alike.

meanings: (bound form) to visit; to call on

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 访 relates to visiting someone to speak with them or ask questions.
方 (fāng) gives a sound distantly related to fǎng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Jìzhě cǎifǎng le nà wèi lǎoshī.
example.fact: 访 usually appears in 访问 (fǎngwèn, 'to visit') and 采访 (cǎifǎng, 'to interview').

etymologyHint: Two shoots 弓 dying to frost 冫

components.note: 弓 here pictures a young, bent shoot rather than a bow.
冫 (ice/frost) repeated twice suggests two young shoots wilting in the cold, giving 弱 its meaning 'weak, fragile.'

example.fact: 弱 is the opposite of 强 (qiáng, 'strong'), and the two are often paired, as in 强弱 (qiángruò, 'strength and weakness').

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 蒙 originally described a climbing plant covering something over.
冡 (méng) gives the sound — an exact match with 蒙's reading méng.

example.pinyin: Tā méng zhù le zìjǐ de yǎnjing.
example.fact: 蒙 means 'to cover' and also names Mongolia (蒙古, Měnggǔ) in Chinese.

components.note: 欠 (breath, an open mouth exhaling) — 歌 relates to the breath used in singing.
哥 (gē) gives the sound — an exact match with 歌's reading gē.

example.pinyin: Tā chànggē chàng de hěn hǎo.
example.fact: 歌 almost always appears in 唱歌 (chànggē, 'to sing') and 歌曲 (gēqǔ, 'song').

components.note: 广 (shelter/building) — 店 names a building used for business.
占 (zhàn) gives a sound distantly related to diàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 店 is used with the measure word 家 (jiā), the same one used for restaurants and companies, as in 一家商店 (yì jiā shāngdiàn, 'a shop').

meanings: sly; crafty; resourceful (variant of 詭|诡[gui3])
etymologyHint: A ghost with a scary face

components.note: The 田-shaped top pictures a large, strange head.
儿-shaped legs below trace a crouching, spindly body, together giving 鬼 the shape of a ghostly figure.

example.english: There is a ghost in this story.
example.fact: 鬼 names ghosts and spirits in folklore, and also appears in 鬼脸 (guǐliǎn, 'funny face') for a playful, non-scary use.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 软 originally described a cart with cushioned, springy wheels, giving a soft ride.
欠 (qiàn) gives a sound distantly related to ruǎn, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 软 is the opposite of 硬 (yìng, 'hard'), and also appears in 软件 (ruǎnjiàn, 'software'), literally 'soft goods.'

etymologyHint: Two hands 八 holding a book 冊

components.note: The 曲-shaped top pictures a bundle of bamboo strips, an ancient book.
八 below pictures two hands supporting the book, giving 典 its meaning 'classic text, standard.'

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì běn cídiǎn.
example.fact: 典 usually appears in 词典 (cídiǎn, 'dictionary') and 字典 (zìdiǎn, 'character dictionary').

components.note: 欠 (to lack) — wanting something you lack ties to 欲's meaning 'desire.'
谷 (gǔ) gives a sound distantly related to yù, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 欲 usually appears in 欲望 (yùwàng, 'desire') and 食欲 (shíyù, 'appetite').

meanings: used in 菩薩|菩萨[pu2 sa4]

example.fact: 萨 rarely stands alone — it mainly appears in 菩萨 (púsà, 'bodhisattva') and in transliterated foreign names and places.

meanings: (bound form) meals (as in 伙食[huo3 shi2])

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伙 relates to people who share meals or work together.
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 伙's reading huǒ.

example.fact: 伙 usually appears in 伙伴 (huǒbàn, 'partner, companion') and 伙食 (huǒshí, 'meals, food'), originally describing people who shared a cooking fire.

meanings: to suffer; to meet with (usu. misfortune)
classifier for events: time, turn, incident

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 遭 relates to something you come across or run into on your way.
曹 (cáo) gives a sound distantly related to zāo, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā zāodào le hěn duō kùnnan.
example.english: He encountered a lot of difficulties.
example.fact: 遭 usually appears in 遭到 (zāodào, 'to encounter, suffer') and 遭遇 (zāoyù, 'to encounter, experience'), almost always describing something unfortunate.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — 盘 names a flat dish or tray.
般 (bān) gives a sound distantly related to pán, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yí gè pánzi.
example.english: There is a plate on the table.
example.fact: 盘 combines with 子 to form 盘子 (pánzi, 'plate'), one of the most common words for tableware.

components.note: 父 (father) — 爸 names a father.
巴 (bā) gives a sound close to bà, sharing the same syllable body and differing only in tone.

example.fact: 爸 is doubled to form 爸爸 (bàba, 'dad'), one of the very first words Chinese children learn to say.

components.note: 广 (wide) — 扩 relates to making something wider or bigger.
扌 also carries a sound value in this simplified character, distantly related to kuò.

example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng kuòdà zìjǐ de gōngsī.
example.english: He wants to expand his own company.
example.fact: 扩 usually appears in 扩大 (kuòdà, 'to expand') and 扩展 (kuòzhǎn, 'to extend, expand').

etymologyHint: A dish 皿 with a lid 羊

components.note: 羊 here pictures a woven lid or cover.
皿 (dish) sits below, together giving 盖 its meaning 'lid, to cover.'

example.english: Please put the lid on the cup.
example.fact: 盖 means 'lid' or 'to cover,' as in 盖子 (gàizi, 'lid') and 覆盖 (fùgài, 'to cover').

etymologyHint: Two hands 廾 playing with a piece of jade 玉; 廾 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 玉 (jade) pictures a treasured object.
廾 pictures two hands, together giving 弄 its meaning 'to play with, to handle, to do.'

example.pinyin: Bié nòng huài wǒ de shǒujī.
example.fact: 弄 is an everyday, informal verb meaning 'to do, to make, to handle,' as in 弄坏 (nòng huài, 'to break') and 弄清楚 (nòng qīngchu, 'to make clear').

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — 雄 originally described the male of a bird species, extending to 'male' generally and 'heroic, grand.'
厷 (gōng) gives a sound distantly related to xióng, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 雄 marks the male of an animal species, as in 雄鸡 (xióngjī, 'rooster'), and also means 'heroic, grand' in words like 英雄 (yīngxióng, 'hero').

components.note: 禾 (grain) — a heavy, ripe stalk of grain standing steady in the field ties to 稳's meaning 'stable, steady.'
㥯 (wěn) gives the sound — an exact match with 稳's reading wěn.

example.fact: 稳 usually appears in 稳定 (wěndìng, 'stable') and 稳重 (wěnzhòng, 'steady, dependable').

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 忘 relates to something slipping from the mind.
亡 (wáng) gives a sound distantly related to wàng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒ wàng le tā de míngzi.
example.fact: 忘 is the everyday verb for 'to forget,' as in 忘记 (wàngjì, 'to forget') and 别忘了 (bié wàng le, 'don't forget').

components.note: 亻 (person) — historically, large numbers were tied to counting groups of people.
乙 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to yì, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: China has a population of 1.4 billion.
example.fact: 亿 is the Chinese unit for a hundred million (100,000,000), used when talking about very large numbers like national populations.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刺 describes the action of piercing or stabbing with something sharp.
朿 (cì) gives the sound — an exact match with 刺's reading cì.

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, zhè duǒ huā yǒu cì.
example.english: Be careful, this flower has thorns.
example.fact: 刺 names a thorn or sharp point, and as a verb means 'to stab, to prick,' as in 刺激 (cìjī, 'to stimulate').

meanings: to hold in one's arms; to embrace

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拥 describes holding someone in your arms.
用 (yòng) gives a sound distantly related to yōng, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 拥 usually appears in 拥抱 (yōngbào, 'to hug') and 拥有 (yōngyǒu, 'to possess, have').

etymologyHint: To walk 走 in someone's footsteps 彳

components.note: 彳 pictures a person's legs walking.
走 (to walk/run) reinforces the idea of movement, giving 徒 its meanings 'on foot' and 'a follower who walks in someone's footsteps.'

example.fact: 徒 usually appears in 徒弟 (túdì, 'apprentice, disciple') and 学徒 (xuétú, 'apprentice').

meanings: used in 姆媽|姆妈[m1 ma1]

components.note: 女 (woman) — 姆 names a woman who cares for children.
母 (mǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 姆's reading mǔ.

example.pinyin: Tāmen qǐng le yí wèi bǎomǔ.
example.fact: 姆 almost never stands alone — it appears in 保姆 (bǎomǔ, 'nanny, babysitter'), one of the few common words that use it.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 杨 names a type of tree, the poplar or willow.

example.pinyin: Hébiān zhòng le hěn duō yángshù.
example.english: Many poplar trees were planted along the riverbank.
example.fact: 杨 names the poplar tree (杨树) and is also one of the most common Chinese surnames.

example.hanzi: 大家一起唱歌，声音很齐。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā yìqǐ chànggē, shēngyīn hěn qí.
example.english: Everyone sang together, and the voices were perfectly in unison.
example.fact: 齐 usually appears in 一齐 (yìqí, 'all at once, together') and 整齐 (zhěngqí, 'neat, orderly').

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赛 originally related to offering valuables, later coming to mean 'to compete.'
宀 (mián) gives a sound distantly related to sài, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Míngtiān yǒu yì chǎng zúqiú bǐsài.
example.english: Tomorrow there is a soccer match.
example.fact: 赛 usually appears in 比赛 (bǐsài, 'competition, match'), one of the most common words for sports and games.

components.note: 走 (to walk/run) — 趣 originally related to hurrying eagerly toward something, extending to 'interesting, of interest.'
取 (qǔ) gives a sound close to qù, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.fact: 趣 almost always appears in 有趣 (yǒuqù, 'interesting') and 兴趣 (xìngqù, 'interest').

components.note: The outline pictures a bent, curved container or musical instrument, giving 曲 its meaning 'crooked, bent' and, by extension, 'a tune.'

example.fact: 曲 means 'bent, crooked' in words like 曲折 (qūzhé, 'winding, twisting'), and separately means 'a song or tune' when read qǔ, as in 歌曲 (gēqǔ).

meanings: classifier for knife cuts or stabs

example.english: Mom uses a knife to cut vegetables.
example.fact: 刀 is the basic word for 'knife' and also the radical (刂) found in many characters related to cutting, like 切 and 别.

meanings: bed; bottom (of rivers, oceans, gardens etc)
etymologyHint: A house 广 made out of wood 木; 广 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 广 (shelter) suggests a piece of furniture kept indoors.
木 (wood) — early beds were built from wood, giving 床 its meaning.

example.pinyin: Tā tǎng zài chuáng shàng shuìjiào.
example.english: He is lying on the bed sleeping.
example.fact: 床 is measured with 张 (zhāng) in some regions but usually just counted directly, as in 一张床 (yì zhāng chuáng, 'a bed').

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迎 describes walking out to meet and welcome someone.
卬 (áng) gives a sound distantly related to yíng, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: We're going to the airport to welcome him.
example.fact: 迎 usually appears in 欢迎 (huānyíng, 'welcome') and 迎接 (yíngjiē, 'to greet, receive').

meanings: (of an object or substance) to feel cold

components.note: 冫 pictures ice crystals forming.
水 (water) sits beside it, together showing water turned to ice.

example.fact: 冰 names ice and also describes something ice-cold, as in 冰水 (bīngshuǐ, 'ice water') and 冰淇淋 (bīngqílín, 'ice cream').

etymologyHint: A tiger 虍 stalking in the bushes 业

components.note: 虍 (tiger) pictures a big cat.
业 pictures tall grass or a hilltop, together suggesting a hollow, empty den — giving 虚 its meaning 'empty, false.'

example.pinyin: Tā shuō de huà shì xūjiǎ de.
example.fact: 虚 usually appears in 虚假 (xūjiǎ, 'false, fake') and 谦虚 (qiānxū, 'modest'), describing something empty of truth or an attitude of humility.

components.note: 王 (jade, written without its dot) — 玩 originally meant to handle and admire a piece of jade, extending to 'to play, to have fun.'
元 (yuán) gives a sound distantly related to wán, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: The children are playing in the park.
example.fact: 玩 is the everyday verb for 'to play' or 'to have fun,' as in 玩游戏 (wán yóuxì, 'to play a game').

etymologyHint: Chopping 斤 wood 木; 斤 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 木 (wood) — the thing being split apart.
斤 pictures an axe, the tool used to chop the wood, giving 析 its meaning 'to split, to analyze.'

example.hanzi: 老师帮我们分析这个问题。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī bāng wǒmen fēnxī zhège wèntí.
example.english: The teacher helps us analyze this problem.
example.fact: 析 almost always appears in 分析 (fēnxī, 'to analyze'), from its original meaning of splitting wood apart piece by piece.

components.note: 穴 (hole/cave) — 窗 originally described an opening for light and air.
囱 (cōng) gives a sound distantly related to chuāng, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 窗 combines with 户 to form 窗户 (chuānghu, 'window'), the everyday word used in most households.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — 醒 originally described sobering up from drink, extending to 'to wake up.'
星 (xīng) gives a sound close to xǐng, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang qī diǎn xǐng le.
example.english: I woke up at seven in the morning.
example.fact: 醒 usually appears in 醒来 (xǐnglái, 'to wake up') and 睡醒 (shuìxǐng, 'to wake from sleep').

etymologyHint: A woman 女 holding a broom 十 in her hand 彐

components.note: 女 (woman) sits at the base of the character.
彐-shaped strokes above picture a hand holding a broom, an old image of a wife managing the household.

example.fact: 妻 usually appears in 妻子 (qīzi, 'wife'), and is often paired with 夫 (fū, 'husband') in 夫妻 (fūqī, 'husband and wife').

meanings: (bound form) to penetrate; to seep through

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 透 relates to moving all the way through something.
秀 (xiù) gives a sound distantly related to tòu, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: Sunlight shines in through the window.
example.fact: 透 usually appears in 透过 (tòuguò, 'through, via') and 看透 (kàntòu, 'to see through, understand fully').

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 购 relates to spending money to buy something.
勾 (gōu) gives a sound close to gòu, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.fact: 购 usually appears in 购物 (gòuwù, 'to shop') and 购买 (gòumǎi, 'to purchase').

etymologyHint: One man 夫 replacing another; 日 provides the pronunciation

components.note: 夫 (man) is shown twice, side by side, one man standing in for another.
日 sits below, together giving 替 its meaning 'to replace, to substitute.'

example.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ tì nǐ qù ma?
example.english: Can I go in your place?
example.fact: 替 means 'to replace, to substitute for,' as in 代替 (dàitì, 'to replace') and 替代 (tìdài, 'to substitute').

components.note: 土 (earth) — 塞 relates to blocking a gap or opening, as with packed earth.

example.english: There's a traffic jam on the road.
example.fact: 塞 usually appears in 塞车 (sāichē, 'traffic jam') and 堵塞 (dǔsè, 'to block up'), both about things being jammed or blocked.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 努 relates to exerting effort and strength.
奴 (nú) gives a sound close to nǔ, sharing the same syllable body and differing only in tone.

example.fact: 努 almost always appears in 努力 (nǔlì, 'to make an effort, work hard'), one of the most common words for encouraging effort.

etymologyHint: A person 亻 leaning against a tree 木

components.note: 亻 (person) leans to the side.
木 (tree) — a person resting against a tree gave 休 its meaning 'to rest.'

example.fact: 休 almost always appears in 休息 (xiūxi, 'to rest'), one of the most common words in daily conversation.

etymologyHint: A tiger 虍 standing on a rock 几; 虍 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 虍 pictures a tiger's head and stripes.
几 below pictures its legs and tail, together giving a full picture of a tiger.

example.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu yì zhī lǎohǔ.
example.english: There is a tiger in the zoo.
example.fact: 虎 combines with 老 to form 老虎 (lǎohǔ, 'tiger'), and is also one of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.

meanings: abbr. for Yangzhou 揚州|扬州[Yang2 zhou1] in Jiangsu

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 扬 describes raising or scattering something with the hand.
昜 (yáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 扬's reading yáng.

example.fact: 扬 usually appears in 表扬 (biǎoyáng, 'to praise') and 飘扬 (piāoyáng, 'to flutter, wave'), as of a flag in the wind.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 途 names a road or path traveled on.
余 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tú, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我们在路途中休息一下。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài lùtú zhōng xiūxi yíxià.
example.english: We took a rest partway through the journey.
example.fact: 途 usually appears in 路途 (lùtú, 'journey, route') and 用途 (yòngtú, 'use, purpose').

example.pinyin: Jūnduì qīnzhàn le zhè piàn tǔdì.
example.english: The army invaded and occupied this piece of land.
example.fact: 侵 usually appears in 侵略 (qīnlüè, 'to invade') and 侵占 (qīnzhàn, 'to invade and occupy').

etymologyHint: A man 刂 in jail 开

components.note: 开-shaped bars picture a cell or restraint.
刂 (knife) adds the idea of physical punishment, giving 刑 its meaning 'punishment, penalty.'

example.english: This is stipulated by criminal law.
example.fact: 刑 usually appears in 刑法 (xíngfǎ, 'criminal law') and 判刑 (pànxíng, 'to sentence someone').

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 绿 originally described a shade of green-dyed silk.
录 (lù) gives a sound close to lǜ, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.fact: 绿 is the standard word for the color green, as in 绿色 (lǜsè, 'green') and 绿茶 (lǜchá, 'green tea').

etymologyHint: Older brother 儿 speaking 口 to younger ones

components.note: 口 (mouth) pictures someone speaking.
儿 (person) below gives the shape of a person, together showing an elder brother speaking to his siblings.

example.fact: 兄 usually appears in 兄弟 (xiōngdì, 'brothers') and 兄长 (xiōngzhǎng, 'elder brother'), both more formal than the everyday 哥哥.

etymologyHint: To walk 辶 quickly 卂; 卂 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迅 relates to fast movement.
卂 pictures something darting forward quickly, giving 迅 its meaning 'rapid, fast.'

example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng yǔ lái de hěn xùnsù.
example.fact: 迅 almost always appears in 迅速 (xùnsù, 'rapid, swift'), describing something happening fast.

etymologyHint: A man 大 wrapped in a long 镸 cloth

components.note: 大 (big, a person with arms and legs spread) pictures a person.
镸 (long) pictures a long piece of cloth wrapped around them, giving 套 its meaning 'cover, case.'

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yí tào yīfu.
example.english: I bought a set of clothes.
example.fact: 套 is a measure word for matching sets, like 一套衣服 (yí tào yīfu, 'a set of clothes') or 一套房子 (a suite of rooms).

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 贸 relates to trade and commerce.
卯 (mǎo) gives a sound distantly related to mào, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这两个国家有很多贸易。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè guójiā yǒu hěn duō màoyì.
example.english: These two countries have a lot of trade.
example.fact: 贸 almost always appears in 贸易 (màoyì, 'trade, commerce'), a key word in economic news.

components.note: 十 here relates to completeness, since 十 (ten) is a round, whole number.
比 (bǐ) gives a sound distantly related to bì, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 毕 almost always appears in 毕业 (bìyè, 'to graduate'), one of the most common words for students.
唯 almost always appears in 唯一 (wéiyī, 'only, sole'), describing something that has no alternative.

etymologyHint: Water flowing 人 from a spring 口 through a valley 八

components.note: 八-shaped strokes at the top picture the sloping walls of a valley.
口 below pictures a spring or opening where water flows out, giving 谷 its meaning 'valley.'

example.english: It's very quiet in the valley.
example.fact: 谷 usually appears in 山谷 (shāngǔ, 'valley'), and Silicon Valley is translated as 硅谷 (Guīgǔ) in Chinese.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 轮 names the wheel of a vehicle.
仑 (lún) gives the sound — an exact match with 轮's reading lún.

example.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē yǒu sì gè lúnzi.
example.fact: 轮 combines with 子 to form 轮子 (lúnzi, 'wheel'), and also appears in 轮流 (lúnliú, 'to take turns').

etymologyHint: A stable 广 where carriages 车 are parked

components.note: 广 (shelter) pictures a roofed building.
车 (cart) sits inside, together giving 库 its meaning 'storehouse, warehouse.'

example.pinyin: Dōngxi dōu fàng zài cāngkù lǐ.
example.english: The things are all stored in the warehouse.
example.fact: 库 usually appears in 仓库 (cāngkù, 'warehouse') and 车库 (chēkù, 'garage').

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迹 names the trace left behind by walking.
亦 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to jī, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Xuědì shàng yǒu hěn duō jiǎojī.
example.english: There are many footprints on the snowy ground.
example.fact: 迹 usually appears in 痕迹 (hénjī, 'trace, mark') and 古迹 (gǔjī, 'historic site').

components.note: 尢 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 尤's reading yóu.

example.fact: 尤 almost always appears in 尤其 (yóuqí, 'especially, particularly'), used to single out one thing among several.

etymologyHint: To stand up 立 to a foe 兄

components.note: 立 (to stand) pictures a person standing firm.
兄 (elder brother, here a rival) suggests standing up against someone, giving 竞 its meaning 'to compete, to contend.'

example.english: They are competing for this position.
example.fact: 竞 usually appears in 竞争 (jìngzhēng, 'to compete') and 竞赛 (jìngsài, 'competition, contest').

components.note: 行 (to go/walk) — 街 names a road where people walk and travel.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to jiē, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē shàng yǒu hěn duō shāngdiàn.
example.english: There are many shops on this street.
example.fact: 街 is the common word for 'street,' as in 逛街 (guàngjiē, 'to go window-shopping, wander the streets').

meanings: (bound form) of short duration; hasty; rapid
(bound form) to hasten; to hurry; to urge
etymologyHint: Someone 亻 on your heels 足; 足 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 亻 (person) stands to the side.
足 (foot) pictures someone following close on your heels, giving 促 its meaning 'to urge, to press.'

example.fact: 促 usually appears in 促进 (cùjìn, 'to promote, boost') and 催促 (cuīcù, 'to urge, hurry someone').

etymologyHint: A foot on the road 㢟 stopped in its tracks 丿

components.note: 㢟 pictures a foot moving along a long road.
丿 marks a pause or stop in that movement, giving 延 its meaning 'to delay, to extend.'

example.pinyin: Huìyì yánchí le yí gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: The meeting was delayed by an hour.
example.fact: 延 usually appears in 延迟 (yánchí, 'to delay') and 延长 (yáncháng, 'to extend, prolong').

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 震 originally described thunder shaking the sky along with a storm.
辰 (chén) gives a sound distantly related to zhèn, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: There was an earthquake last night.
example.fact: 震 almost always appears in 地震 (dìzhèn, 'earthquake'), the shaking of the ground.

etymologyHint: Two hands 廾 discarding a dead, swaddled baby 亠厶

components.note: 亠厶-shaped top pictures a bundled object being cast away.
廾 (two hands) below shows the act of throwing it out, giving 弃 its meaning 'to abandon, discard.'

example.fact: 弃 almost always appears in 放弃 (fàngqì, 'to give up, abandon'), a very common word of encouragement.

meanings: (used for an unspecified person or thing)
first (in a list, as a party to a contract etc)

example.pinyin: Tā páimíng dì yī, shì jiǎděng.
example.english: He ranked first, in the top grade.
example.fact: 甲 is the first of the 10 heavenly stems (天干) used for ordering, similar to how 'A' is used in English, and also means 'shell' or 'armor.'

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伟 describes a person of great, extraordinary character.
韦 (wéi) gives a sound close to wěi, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 他是一位伟大的科学家。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi wěidà de kēxuéjiā.
example.fact: 伟 almost always appears in 伟大 (wěidà, 'great, mighty'), used for people or achievements of great importance.

etymologyHint: Hemp plants 林 growing in a greenhouse 广

components.note: 广 (shelter) pictures a drying shed.
林-shaped strokes below picture hemp fibers hung to dry, giving 麻 its meaning 'hemp.'

example.english: This dish is a bit spicy and numbing.
example.fact: 麻 names hemp fiber and also describes a numbing sensation, as in 麻辣 (málà, 'spicy and numbing'), a famous flavor of Sichuan cuisine.

meanings: short name for Sichuan 四川[Si4 chuan1]

components.note: The three vertical strokes trace the flowing lines of a river between its banks.

example.english: Sichuan's hot pot is very famous.
example.fact: 川 means 'river' and is also the short name for Sichuan province (四川), literally 'four rivers.'

meanings: old name for Shanghai 上海[Shang4 hai3]

components.note: The character traces a jagged bolt of lightning splitting the sky, later borrowed for the abstract meaning 'to state, to extend.'

example.pinyin: Wǒ yào shēnqǐng yì zhāng hùzhào.
example.english: I need to apply for a passport.
example.fact: 申 usually appears in 申请 (shēnqǐng, 'to apply') and is also the old name for Shanghai, seen in its car license plates (沪).

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 缓 originally described a loosened, slackened thread, extending to 'slow, unhurried.'
爰 (yuán) gives a sound distantly related to huǎn, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: Please slow down the car's speed.
example.fact: 缓 usually appears in 缓慢 (huǎnmàn, 'slow') and 缓解 (huǎnjiě, 'to relieve, ease').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 潜 describes hiding beneath the surface of water.
替 (tì) gives a sound distantly related to qián, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 潜 almost always appears in 潜水 (qiánshuǐ, 'to dive') and 潜力 (qiánlì, 'potential').

etymologyHint: A man 人 just glimpsed through a door 门

components.note: 门 (door) frames the scene.
人 (person) glimpsed briefly inside, giving 闪 its meaning 'to flash, to dodge quickly.'

example.english: There was a flash in the sky.
example.fact: 闪 describes a quick flash, as in 闪电 (shǎndiàn, 'lightning'), and also means 'to dodge,' as in 闪开 (shǎnkāi, 'get out of the way').

meanings: (literary) to carry out (a plan or intrigue etc)
etymologyHint: A street vendor talks 口 incessantly, like a bird 隹

components.note: 隹 (bird) suggests constant chatter, like a bird calling.
口 (mouth) below pictures a vendor calling out to sell goods, giving 售 its meaning 'to sell.'

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn zài chūshòu shuǐguǒ.
example.fact: 售 usually appears in 出售 (chūshòu, 'to sell') and 售票员 (shòupiàoyuán, 'ticket seller').

components.note: 火 (fire) — 灯 names a lamp, which once gave light through a small flame.
丁 (dīng) gives a sound distantly related to dēng, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 灯 is the everyday word for 'lamp, light,' as in 台灯 (táidēng, 'desk lamp') and 红灯 (hóngdēng, 'red light').

etymologyHint: A metal 钅 pin 十

components.note: 钅 (metal) shows what the object is made of.
十 pictures a thin, straight pin, giving 针 its meaning 'needle.'

example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi wǒ dǎ le yì zhēn.
example.english: The doctor gave me an injection.
example.fact: 针 names needles used for sewing, acupuncture (针灸, zhēnjiǔ), and medical injections (打针, dǎzhēn).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哲 relates to wise speech from a sage.
折 (zhé) gives the sound — an exact match with 哲's reading zhé.

example.fact: 哲 almost always appears in 哲学 (zhéxué, 'philosophy'), the study of wisdom and fundamental questions.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 络 relates to threads woven together into a net or web.
各 (gè) gives a sound distantly related to luò, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: I use the internet to look up information.
example.fact: 络 almost always appears in 网络 (wǎngluò, 'network, internet'), one of the most common tech words.

meanings: to press against; to support; to prop up

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 抵 describes pushing back or propping something up with the hand.
氐 (dī) gives a sound close to dǐ, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.fact: 抵 usually appears in 抵抗 (dǐkàng, 'to resist') and 抵达 (dǐdá, 'to arrive').

etymologyHint: The color of the sap 一 of some trees 木

components.note: 木 (tree) forms the base of the character.
一 marks the trunk's red-colored heartwood, giving 朱 its meaning 'vermilion, reddish.'

example.fact: 朱 names a bright red color, vermilion, and is also a common Chinese surname, shared by the founding emperor of the Ming dynasty, Zhu Yuanzhang.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 埃 names fine dust or dirt.
矣 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to āi, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yì céng āi.
example.english: There is a layer of dust on the table.
example.fact: 埃 rarely stands alone in everyday speech; it also names the ancient civilization of Egypt, 埃及 (Āijí), in transliteration.

etymologyHint: To wrap 包 in one's arms 扌; 包 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows the action is done with the arms.
包 (to wrap) — wrapping your arms around something gives 抱 its meaning 'to hold, to hug.'

example.english: The mom is holding the child in her arms.
example.fact: 抱 usually appears in 拥抱 (yōngbào, 'to hug') and 抱歉 (bàoqiàn, 'to apologize'), the second being an extended, figurative use.

components.note: 壴 pictures a drum standing on a base.
支 (zhī) gives a sound distantly related to gǔ, having drifted apart over time; it also pictures a hand holding a drumstick.

example.fact: 鼓 names the drum, and also means 'to encourage,' as in 鼓励 (gǔlì, 'to encourage').

components.note: 木 (tree) — 植 relates to planting trees and other plants.
直 (zhí) gives the sound — an exact match with 植's reading zhí.

example.hanzi: 我们在花园里种植花草。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài huāyuán lǐ zhòngzhí huācǎo.
example.english: We plant flowers and grass in the garden.
example.fact: 植 usually appears in 植物 (zhíwù, 'plant') and 种植 (zhòngzhí, 'to plant, cultivate').

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 纯 originally described unmixed, undyed silk thread, extending to 'pure, unmixed.'
屯 (tún) gives a sound distantly related to chún, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì chún mián de.
example.english: This piece of clothing is pure cotton.
example.fact: 纯 usually appears in 纯棉 (chún mián, 'pure cotton') and 单纯 (dānchún, 'simple, pure').

meanings: the Xia or Hsia dynasty c. 2000 BC

example.fact: 夏 almost always appears in 夏天 (xiàtiān, 'summer'), and also names China's first recorded dynasty, the Xia (夏朝).

etymologyHint: A knife 刃 piercing the heart 心; 刃 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 刃 (blade) pictures something sharp and painful.
心 (heart) below suggests bearing pain in one's heart, giving 忍 its meaning 'to endure.'

example.pinyin: Tā rěn bú zhù xiào le.
example.fact: 忍 usually appears in 忍不住 (rěn bú zhù, 'can't help, can't bear it') and 忍耐 (rěnnài, 'to endure, be patient').

components.note: The character traces a person's head and neck seen from the side; 'page' is a later, borrowed meaning.

example.pinyin: Qǐng fān dào dì èrshí yè.
example.fact: 页 is the everyday word for 'page,' and also appears in 网页 (wǎngyè, 'webpage').

example.hanzi: 他是一个很杰出的运动员。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè hěn jiéchū de yùndòngyuán.
example.fact: 杰 almost always appears in 杰出 (jiéchū, 'outstanding'), and is also a common character in Chinese given names.

meanings: short name for Guiyang 貴陽|贵阳[Gui4 yang2]
etymologyHint: A strong  巩 bamboo ⺮ building; ⺮ also provides the pronunciation

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) recalls bamboo poles used in early construction.
巩 (strong, firm) reinforces the idea of a sturdy structure, giving 筑 its meaning 'to build.'

example.pinyin: Tāmen zài jiànzhù yí zuò dàlóu.
example.english: They are constructing a large building.
example.fact: 筑 almost always appears in 建筑 (jiànzhù, 'to build, construct; a building'), a key word in architecture and construction.

meanings: to break (a stick, a bone etc)
(bound form) to sustain a loss (in business)
etymologyHint: A hand 扌 wielding an axe 斤

components.note: 扌 (hand) does the action.
斤 (axe) — chopping and snapping something in two gives 折 its meaning 'to break, to bend.'

example.fact: 折 means 'to break, to bend' and also describes discounts, as in 打折 (dǎzhé, 'to give a discount').

meanings: used in 鄭重|郑重[zheng4 zhong4]
etymologyHint: A city 阝 guarding a pass 关

components.note: 关 (pass, gate) marks a guarded mountain pass.
阝 (city/mound) names a settlement near it, giving 郑 its use as a place name and surname.

example.fact: 郑 is a common Chinese surname, and also appears in 郑重 (zhèngzhòng, 'solemn, serious').

etymologyHint: A sea shell, once used as currency

components.note: The character traces the rounded shell and radiating lines of a cowrie shell, once used as ancient Chinese currency.

example.english: There are a lot of seashells at the beach.
example.fact: 贝 combines with 壳 to form 贝壳 (bèiké, 'seashell'), and appears as a component in many money-related characters, like 买 and 贵.

etymologyHint: A hand 寸 making an offering of wine 酋

components.note: 酋 pictures a jar of wine.
寸 (hand) below offers it up respectfully, giving 尊 its meaning 'to respect, to honor.'

example.fact: 尊 usually appears in 尊重 (zūnzhòng, 'to respect') and 尊敬 (zūnjìng, 'to esteem, honor').
吴 is a common Chinese surname, and also names an ancient state during the Warring States period and the Three Kingdoms era.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 秀 originally described a grain plant coming into flower, extending to 'elegant, outstanding.'

example.fact: 秀 usually appears in 优秀 (yōuxiù, 'outstanding, excellent') and 秀气 (xiùqi, 'delicate, refined').

components.note: 氵 (water) — 混 originally described muddy, mixed water.
昆 (kūn) gives a sound distantly related to hùn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 请不要把这两件事混在一起。
example.pinyin: Qǐng búyào bǎ zhè liǎng jiàn shì hùn zài yìqǐ.
example.english: Please don't mix up these two matters.
example.fact: 混 usually appears in 混合 (hùnhé, 'to mix') and 混乱 (hùnluàn, 'chaos, confusion').

meanings: state official or subject in dynastic China
I, your servant (used in addressing the sovereign)

example.fact: 臣 named a court official or minister in dynastic China, and appears in historical dramas in words like 大臣 (dàchén, 'high minister').

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — 雅 originally named a type of crow, later borrowed for the unrelated meaning 'elegant, refined.'
牙 (yá) gives a sound close to yǎ, sharing the same syllable body and differing only in tone.

example.fact: 雅 usually appears in 雅致 (yǎzhì, 'elegant') and 优雅 (yōuyǎ, 'graceful').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 振 describes shaking or waving something with the hand.
辰 (chén) gives a sound distantly related to zhèn, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: This news is uplifting to people.
example.fact: 振 usually appears in 振奋 (zhènfèn, 'to stir, uplift') and 振动 (zhèndòng, 'to vibrate').

etymologyHint: Water 氵 and wine 九 mixed in a wooden 木 bowl

components.note: 木 (wood) pictures a wooden dyeing vat.
氿-shaped strokes above picture liquid dye poured into it, giving 染 its meaning 'to dye.'

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ tóufa rǎn chéng le hóngsè.
example.fact: 染 usually appears in 染色 (rǎnsè, 'to dye') and 感染 (gǎnrǎn, 'to become infected'), extending the idea of dye spreading to disease spreading.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — 盛 relates to filling a dish or vessel to abundance.
成 (chéng) gives a sound distantly related to shèng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de huā kāi de hěn shèng.
example.english: The flowers here are blooming abundantly.
example.fact: 盛 usually appears in 盛开 (shèngkāi, 'to bloom abundantly') and 丰盛 (fēngshèng, 'sumptuous, abundant').

components.note: 心 (heart) — 怒 relates to strong feeling in the heart: anger.
奴 (nú) gives a sound close to nù, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.english: He is very angry, full of rage.
example.fact: 怒 usually appears in 愤怒 (fènnù, 'angry, furious') and 怒气 (nùqì, 'anger').

etymologyHint: A hand 舛 holding a fan

components.note: 無-shaped top pictures a dancer holding decorated sleeves or fans.
舛 below pictures a pair of feet, together giving 舞 its meaning 'to dance.'

example.pinyin: Tā tiàowǔ tiào de hěn hǎo.
example.fact: 舞 almost always appears in 跳舞 (tiàowǔ, 'to dance') and 舞蹈 (wǔdǎo, 'dance').

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — 圆 describes a shape fully enclosed by a curved line: a circle.
员 (yuán) gives the sound — an exact match with 圆's reading yuán.

example.fact: 圆 describes round shapes, and a full moon (圆月, yuányuè) is a traditional symbol of family reunion at Mid-Autumn Festival.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 搞 is a general verb for doing or handling something with the hands.
高 (gāo) gives a sound close to gǎo, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.fact: 搞 is a very common, informal verb meaning 'to do, to make,' used in casual speech more than 做 in many contexts.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — 狂 originally described a mad, rabid dog, extending to 'wild, crazy.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound distantly related to kuáng, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: A wild wind is blowing outside.
example.fact: 狂 usually appears in 狂风 (kuángfēng, 'wild wind') and 疯狂 (fēngkuáng, 'crazy, wild').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 措 describes arranging or handling something.
昔 (xī) gives a sound distantly related to cuò, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ cǎiqǔ le xīn de cuòshī.
example.fact: 措 almost always appears in 措施 (cuòshī, 'measure, step') and 不知所措 (bù zhī suǒ cuò, 'to not know what to do').

components.note: 女 (woman) — in ancient China, family names traced descent through the mother's line, tying 姓 to the woman radical.
生 (shēng) gives a sound distantly related to xìng, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 姓 is the word for 'surname,' and 你姓什么 (Nǐ xìng shénme?) is one of the first questions Chinese learners learn to ask.

components.note: 歹 (death/bad) — 残 relates to damage, destruction, and injury.
戋 (jiān) gives a sound distantly related to cán, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū zhǐ shèng xià cányè.
example.english: Only damaged pages remain of this book.
example.fact: 残 usually appears in 残忍 (cánrěn, 'cruel') and 残疾 (cánjí, 'disability').

etymologyHint: The time of year when farmers would burn 禾 crops 火

components.note: 禾 (grain) points to the harvest season.
火 (fire) recalls burning off crop stubble after harvest, giving 秋 its meaning 'autumn.'

example.pinyin: Qiūtiān de shùyè shì huángsè de.
example.fact: 秋 names the autumn season, and China's Mid-Autumn Festival, 中秋节 (Zhōngqiū Jié), falls in this season.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 培 originally described banking up soil around a plant's roots, extending to 'to cultivate, nurture.'
咅 (pǒu) gives a sound distantly related to péi, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Xuéxiào péiyǎng le hěn duō réncái.
example.english: The school has cultivated a lot of talented people.
example.fact: 培 almost always appears in 培养 (péiyǎng, 'to cultivate, nurture') and 培训 (péixùn, 'to train').

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迷 originally described losing one's way while walking, extending to 'confused, obsessed.'
米 (mǐ) gives a sound distantly related to mí, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè zúqiú mí.
example.fact: 迷 names a devoted fan, as in 球迷 (qiúmí, 'sports fan'), and also means 'to lose one's way' or 'to be infatuated,' as in 迷路 (mílù, 'to get lost').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诚 relates to speaking honestly and sincerely.
成 (chéng) gives the sound — an exact match with 诚's reading chéng.

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè chéngshí de rén.
example.fact: 诚 usually appears in 诚实 (chéngshí, 'honest') and 真诚 (zhēnchéng, 'sincere').

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宽 originally described a spacious house.
苋 (xiàn) gives a sound distantly related to kuān, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 宽 usually appears in 宽阔 (kuānkuò, 'broad, spacious') and 宽容 (kuānróng, 'tolerant').

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宇 originally named the eaves of a house, extending outward in meaning to 'the universe.'
于 (yú) gives a sound close to yǔ, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.fact: 宇 almost always appears in 宇宙 (yǔzhòu, 'universe, cosmos') and 宇航员 (yǔhángyuán, 'astronaut').

components.note: 犭 (dog) — 猛 originally described a fierce dog, extending to 'fierce, violent' generally.
孟 (mèng) gives a sound close to měng, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.english: The wind outside is very fierce.
example.fact: 猛 usually appears in 猛烈 (měngliè, 'fierce, violent') and 凶猛 (xiōngměng, 'ferocious').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 摆 describes placing or swinging something with the hand.
罢 (bà) gives a sound distantly related to bǎi, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū bǎi zài zhuōzi shàng.
example.english: Please place the book on the table.
example.fact: 摆 usually appears in 摆放 (bǎifàng, 'to place, arrange') and 摇摆 (yáobǎi, 'to sway, swing').

components.note: 木 (tree) — 梅 names the plum tree.
每 (měi) gives a sound close to méi, sharing the same syllable body and differing only in tone.

example.fact: 梅 names the plum tree, and its flower, 梅花 (méihuā), is admired in Chinese culture for blooming even in cold winter.

etymologyHint: A man using a tool 殳 to strike 工 a clay vessel 臼

components.note: 臼 pictures a clay mortar or vessel.
殳 (a tool, held in a hand) strikes it, giving 毁 its meaning 'to destroy, to smash.'

example.pinyin: Dàhuǒ huǐ le zhè zuò fángzi.
example.fact: 毁 usually appears in 毁坏 (huǐhuài, 'to destroy') and 摧毁 (cuīhuǐ, 'to demolish').

etymologyHint: To extend your confidence 申 to another person 亻; 申 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 亻 (person) does the action.
申 pictures something stretched out straight, like a bolt of lightning, giving 伸 its meaning 'to extend, to stretch.'

example.english: He reached out his hand to take the book.
example.fact: 伸 usually appears in 伸手 (shēn shǒu, 'to reach out one's hand') and 伸展 (shēnzhǎn, 'to stretch, extend').

components.note: 手 (hand) — 摩 describes rubbing something with the hand.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: He rubbed his hands together to warm up.
example.fact: 摩 almost always appears in 摩擦 (mócā, 'friction, to rub'), a word used in both physics and everyday speech.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — 盟 originally described an oath sworn over a sacrificial dish.
明 (míng) gives a sound distantly related to méng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Liǎng gè guójiā jiéchéng le tóngméng.
example.english: The two countries formed an alliance.
example.fact: 盟 usually appears in 同盟 (tóngméng, 'alliance') and 联盟 (liánméng, 'union, league').

etymologyHint: The top 一 of a tree 木

components.note: 木 (tree) forms the base.
一 marks the very top of the tree, giving 末 its meaning 'end, tip, final.'

example.hanzi: 这个学期快要结束了，就在月末。
example.pinyin: Zhège xuéqī kuàiyào jiéshù le, jiù zài yuèmò.
example.english: This semester is about to end, right at the end of the month.
example.fact: 末 usually appears in 周末 (zhōumò, 'weekend') and 月末 (yuèmò, 'end of the month').

components.note: The curved shape traces the swollen body of a pregnant woman, a meaning this literary character no longer carries directly.

example.pinyin: Zhè cái shì chénggōng zhī dào.
example.english: This is truly the way to success.
example.fact: 乃 is a literary word meaning 'then, thus,' rarely used in everyday speech but common in classical texts and set phrases.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 悲 relates to a heavy, sorrowful heart.
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to bēi, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè bēishāng de gùshi.
example.fact: 悲 usually appears in 悲伤 (bēishāng, 'sad, sorrowful') and 悲剧 (bēijù, 'tragedy').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拍 describes striking something lightly with the hand.
白 (bái) gives a sound distantly related to pāi, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā pāi le yì zhāng zhàopiàn.
example.fact: 拍 usually appears in 拍照 (pāizhào, 'to take a photo') and 拍手 (pāishǒu, 'to clap hands').

meanings: the 4th of the 10 Heavenly Stems 天干[tian1 gan1]

components.note: The character traces the head and shaft of a simple nail, a shape later borrowed for other meanings.

example.fact: 丁 is the 4th of the 10 Heavenly Stems used for ordering, and also names a small piece cut into cubes, as in 土豆丁 (tǔdòu dīng, 'diced potato').
赵 is a common Chinese surname, and also names one of the seven major states of the Warring States period.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 硬 describes something as hard and firm as stone.
更 (gèng) gives a sound distantly related to yìng, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 硬 is the opposite of 软 (ruǎn, 'soft'), and also appears in 硬件 (yìngjiàn, 'hardware').

meanings: simplified form of KangXi radical number 199
etymologyHint: Simplified form of 麦; grains 來 ready to be harvested 夂

components.note: 龶-shaped top pictures a ripe stalk of grain.
夂 below pictures roots or a foot, together giving 麦 its meaning 'wheat.'

example.pinyin: Zhè piàn dì zhòng de shì xiǎomài.
example.english: This field is planted with wheat.
example.fact: 麦 names wheat and appears in 麦当劳 (Màidāngláo, 'McDonald's'), a transliteration built from this character.

meanings: Chiang Kai-shek 蔣介石|蒋介石[Jiang3 Jie4 shi2]

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 蒋 originally named a type of water plant.
将 (jiāng) gives a sound close to jiǎng, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.

example.fact: 蒋 is a Chinese surname, most widely known from Chiang Kai-shek (蔣介石), a major 20th-century political and military leader.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 操 relates to controlling or handling something.
喿 (zào) gives a sound distantly related to cāo, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: We do morning exercises every day.
example.fact: 操 usually appears in 操作 (cāozuò, 'to operate') and 早操 (zǎocāo, 'morning exercises').

components.note: 耳 (ear) — the original meaning of 耶 is unrelated to its modern use, which is mainly phonetic.
阝 (a place-name element) gives a sound distantly related to yé, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 耶稣是基督教的重要人物。
example.pinyin: Yēsū shì Jīdūjiào de zhòngyào rénwù.
example.english: Jesus is an important figure in Christianity.
example.fact: 耶 is used mainly for its sound in transliterations, most famously in 耶稣 (Yēsū, 'Jesus') and 耶路撒冷 (Yēlùsālěng, 'Jerusalem').

components.note: 阝 (mound/hill) — 阻 originally described a hill or ridge blocking one's path.
且 (qiě) gives a sound distantly related to zǔ, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: The heavy rain stopped us from going out.
example.fact: 阻 usually appears in 阻止 (zǔzhǐ, 'to stop, prevent') and 阻碍 (zǔ'ài, 'to hinder, obstruct').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 订 relates to arranging something through discussion or agreement.
丁 (dīng) gives a sound distantly related to dìng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zài wǎngshàng dìng le yì zhāng piào.
example.fact: 订 usually appears in 订票 (dìngpiào, 'to book a ticket') and 订单 (dìngdān, 'order form').

components.note: 彡 (fine lines, streaks) — 彩 relates to patterns and bright colors.
采 (cǎi) gives the sound — an exact match with 彩's reading cǎi.

example.fact: 彩 usually appears in 彩色 (cǎisè, 'color, colored') and 精彩 (jīngcǎi, 'brilliant, wonderful').

meanings: to draw out; to pull out from in between
to remove part of the whole

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 抽 describes pulling something out with the hand.
由 (yóu) gives a sound distantly related to chōu, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: He opened the drawer to look for the key.
example.fact: 抽 usually appears in 抽屉 (chōuti, 'drawer') and 抽烟 (chōuyān, 'to smoke a cigarette').

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赞 originally related to offering valuables in support of someone.
兟 (shēn) gives a sound distantly related to zàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zànměi le tā de zuòwén.
example.fact: 赞 usually appears in 赞美 (zànměi, 'to praise') and 赞成 (zànchéng, 'to approve, agree with'), and is also the word for a social media 'like.'

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — 魔 names a demon or evil spirit.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这个电影里有一个魔法师。
example.pinyin: Zhège diànyǐng lǐ yǒu yí gè mófǎshī.
example.english: There is a magician in this movie.
example.fact: 魔 usually appears in 魔法 (mófǎ, 'magic') and 魔鬼 (móguǐ, 'devil, demon').
